lines.trans: Did you see my old teacher beam when he saw the green shutters open, Mazen?!
He recognized our old walnut piano through the glass before he took three steps!
And he remembered your name right at the bus station, didn't he, Rami?
Called me Front-Row Notebook before I even lowered the compass welcome sign!
He whispered that his voice is hoarse from talking on the long bus ride.
No wonder he patted his coat pocket—he brought a toast card for us!
First let me bring out my family green guest book opened to May thirty years ago.
And may we lend him brass key number eight from the wooden board for the afternoon?
Room Eight is empty tonight—better yet, Nour, Room Eight is his on the house!
He also handed Ziad a flat wooden parcel wrapped in brown kraft paper at the gate.
Oooh, a flat parcel from a master mapmaker? Do not peek until after cake!
Carry out the brass compass and key number eight—Room Nine is ready for music!

meanings.note: Invariant comparative/superlative of منيح ('good'). Before a noun without ال- it means 'the best' (أحسن نومة 'the best sleep').

examples.trans: This is the best room in the house.
I feel better today.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: خضرا, plural: خضر).

examples.trans: Pass beside the green pharmacy.
Put the green herbs on the eggs.

meanings.note: Polite Jordanian title for any man ('sir / Mr') as well as 'teacher' or 'professor'.

examples.trans: Please have a seat, sir.
Good morning, gentlemen.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بعطي, بيعطي).

examples.trans: Did the shopkeeper give you a receipt?
Give me the breakfast bag, please.

meanings.note: Before an indefinite noun أول means 'first' (أول يوم 'first day'); after a definite noun الأول / الأولى agrees in gender (الصفحة الأولى 'the first page'). Also used adverbially ('first').

examples.trans: Welcome on your first day of work!
Read the first page calmly.

meanings.note: Exclamation of mild surprise or realization ('oh!').

examples.trans: Oh! My glasses are on my head!
Oh, look at the beauty of this ceiling!

meanings.note: Jordan, Syria, Lebanon and Palestine use the old Syriac-derived month names: كانون التاني January ... أيار May ... أيلول September.

examples.trans: My birthday is in May.
In May the weather gets nice in Amman.

meanings.note: Introduces 'that'-clauses with pronoun suffixes (إنه 'that', إني 'that I', إنك 'that you', إنها 'that she/it') and appears in إن شاء الله ('if God wills').

examples.trans: Thank you for coming today.
Do you think that I am a hotel inspector?

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (ببتسم, بيبتسم).

examples.trans: Smile when the bell rings!
He smiled when he saw his brother.

meanings.note: Everyday noun for a person's or place's name; takes possessive endings directly (اسمي my name, اسمك your name).

examples.trans: What is your kind name?
My name is written here in the notebook.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: باصات.

examples.trans: The bus station is close to here.
The bus trip was comfortable.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: بطاقات.

examples.trans: There is a paper tag on the suitcase.
I wrote my name on the card.

meanings.note: Means 'after' (بعد المطر) and with a future span 'in' (بعد أربعين دقيقة 'in forty minutes').

examples.trans: He arrives in forty minutes.
How lovely the sun is after the rain!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: بنية, plural: بنيين).

examples.trans: The brown leather notebook is on the desk.
A clean pair of men's brown shoes.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: بوابات.

examples.trans: The courtyard gate is open for guests.
The taxi stopped outside the gate.

meanings.note: Feminine noun for a navigation compass (بوصلة النحاس 'the brass compass'). Plural: بوصلات.

examples.trans: The brass compass always stays at the front desk.

examples.text: رسمنا بوصلة صغيرة على بطاقة الترحيب.
examples.trans: We drew a small compass on the welcome card.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: بيانوهات.

examples.trans: The sound of the piano is warm and calm.
I learned piano when I was young.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: بيوت.

examples.trans: The old house has a lovely courtyard.
The neighbourhood houses are built of stone.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian possessive word ('belonging to'); agrees in gender: تبع (m.), تبعت (f.), تبعون (pl.).

examples.text: اليوم آخر يوم بأسبوع التجربة تبعك.
examples.trans: Today is the last day of your trial week.
My brother's piano teacher!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: تحيات.

examples.trans: Here is to all our kind neighbours!
He returned the greeting with a warm smile.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بتذكر, بيتذكر).

examples.trans: Remember your three simple sentences.
I can remember them easily.

meanings.note: Nisba adjective from ترحيب ('welcoming'). Feminine: ترحيبية (لوحة ترحيبية 'welcome sign').

examples.text: كتبنا لوحة ترحيبية للضيف قبل ما يوصل.
examples.trans: We wrote a welcome sign for the guest before he arrived.
A welcoming smile is the most important thing at the front desk.

meanings.note: Numeral 'nine'; short form تسع (tisa') before a plural noun (تسع دقايق 'nine minutes').

examples.trans: The quietness in the courtyard is nine out of ten!
She came back in just nine minutes!

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian numeral 'three'; short form تلات (talaat) directly before a plural noun (تلات سنين 'three years').

examples.trans: Three years was a long time.
One, two, three!

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian numeral 'thirty'.

examples.trans: They have given us thirty days in the letter.
The bill is thirty-eight dinars.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian numeral 'eight'; short form تمن (taman) before a plural noun (تمن غرف 'eight rooms').

examples.text: عندنا تمن غرف وتمن مفاتيح نحاس.
examples.trans: We have eight rooms and eight brass keys.
He arrives at eight in the evening.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بجيب, بيجيب).

examples.text: رح أجيب شراشف نظيفة من الخزانة.
examples.trans: I will bring clean sheets from the closet.

examples.text: أي علبة زبدة جبتي يا نور؟
examples.trans: Which tub of butter did you bring, Nour?

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: جاكيتات.

examples.trans: The key is in the right jacket pocket.

examples.text: البس جاكيت دافي قبل ما تطلع.
examples.trans: Put on a warm jacket before you go out.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: جاهزة, plural: جاهزين).

examples.trans: The desk is clean and the keys are ready.
Breakfast is ready in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Collective noun for walnuts; خشب جوز is walnut wood. (Not to be confused with جوز 'husband; pair', a different everyday sense.)

examples.trans: I bought a kilo of walnuts at the market.
The cake has walnuts and honey in it.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: جيب.

examples.trans: Put the key in the coat pocket.
The paper is in my right pocket.

meanings.note: Before a noun or clause حتى means 'even' (حتى والغرفة فاضية 'even when the room is empty').

examples.text: حتى والغرفة فاضية، السلك بيرن مرتين.
examples.trans: Even when the room is empty, the wire rings twice.
Even room four's bell went quiet!

meanings.note: Also used in the warm hospitality phrase على حسابنا ('on our tab / on the house').

examples.trans: The bill is thirty-eight dinars.
The first coffee today is on the house!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: Save the formal talk for later.
That is kind, honest talk.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: خرايط.

examples.trans: Look at the folded map inside the box.
We drew a small map of the street.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أخشاب.

examples.trans: The wooden ceiling is warm and quiet.
This is a hand-carved wooden train.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: خطوات.

examples.trans: I heard footsteps on the wooden stairs.
We walked step by step in the rain.

meanings.note: Very frequent Jordanian verb: خليني ('let me'), خلينا ('let us'), خليك ('stay!'), خلي ('keep/leave').

examples.trans: Let us open the door together.
Hot bread makes people pleasant!

meanings.note: Single hinged panel or leaf of a double window, shutter, or cupboard.

examples.text: فتحنا الدرفة الشمال وبعدين الدرفة اليمين.
examples.trans: We swung open the left shutter leaf and then the right one.

examples.text: كل شباك إله درفتين خشب متينات.
examples.trans: Each window has two sturdy wooden shutter panels.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: دفاتر.

examples.trans: We wrote the name in the booking ledger.
I forgot my leather notebook on the table.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: رحلات.

examples.trans: How was the bus trip today?
We wish you a happy, comfortable journey.

meanings.note: Intensive occupation noun from رسم ('draw/paint'). رسام خرايط means 'mapmaker/cartographer'.

examples.text: رسام الخرايط قعد على طاولة واحد.
examples.trans: The mapmaker sat down at table one.

examples.text: هاد الرسام عمل لوحة رائعة للشارع.
examples.trans: This artist made a wonderful painting of the street.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أرقام.

examples.trans: Here is your key, room number four.
Is there a phone number written on the paper?

meanings.note: Core word in مع السلامة! ('goodbye!', literally 'with safety') and الحمد لله عالسلامة ('glad you arrived safely').

examples.trans: Goodbye, see you tomorrow!
Thank goodness for your safe arrival.

سلّم.gloss: to greet; say hello; hand over

meanings.en: to greet; say hello; hand over
meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بسلم, بيسلم).

examples.trans: Give my regards to Salma in the kitchen!
We hand the suitcase over to its owner on Friday.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: سميكة, plural: سماك).

examples.text: مين ترك هاد المغلف السميك هون؟
examples.trans: Who left this thick envelope here?
Thick stone walls hold the warmth.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: سنين.

examples.trans: The building is eighty years old.
I have not seen him for three years.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb for 'to see, look, check' (بشوف / شاف).

examples.trans: Look inside the suitcase, Nour!
I will see you tomorrow at breakfast.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: صفوف.

examples.trans: We sat in the front row at the concert.
The chairs are arranged in two rows.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أصوات.

examples.trans: I heard the sound of rain on the window.
His voice is calm and polite on the phone.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: ضيوف.

examples.trans: The guests are coming down to breakfast now.
We welcomed every guest with a smile.

meanings.note: Expressive quadriliteral verb (بطبطب / طبطب) meaning 'to pat' a pocket, shoulder, or back.

examples.text: طبطب على جيبة الجاكيت عشان يطمّن.
examples.trans: He patted his coat pocket to reassure himself.
She patted her brother's shoulder with a smile.

meanings.en: to peek; to look out; to drop by briefly
meanings.note: Geminate verb (بطل / طليت) from root ط-ل-ل meaning to peer out or pop in.

examples.trans: The drawings peek out from the edge of the envelope.

examples.text: طل علينا شوي قبل ما تسافر.
examples.trans: Drop by to see us briefly before you travel.

طلع.gloss: to go up; go out; come out; turn out

meanings.en: to go up; go out; come out; turn out
meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بطلع, بيطلع).

examples.text: لفائف القرفة هلا طلعت من الفرن!
examples.trans: The cinnamon rolls just came out of the oven!
Go up the stairs to the third floor.

meanings.note: Before a time noun, طول (tuul) means 'all ... long / throughout' (طول الليل all night long, طول الأسبوع all week).

examples.trans: The rain fell all night long.
Breakfast is free all week long.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: طويلة, plural: طوال).

examples.text: في رجال طويل واقف عند البوابة.
examples.trans: There is a tall man standing by the gate.
Three years was a long time.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بعرف, بيعرف).

examples.trans: I recognized your neat handwriting in two seconds!
Do you know anyone here in Amman?

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: عصور.

examples.trans: We arrived at the guesthouse Monday afternoon.
Late-afternoon tea in the courtyard is a daily ritual.

علطول.gloss: right away; straight; all the time

meanings.en: right away; straight; all the time
meanings.note: Contracted spoken spelling of على طول ('immediately / straight ahead / always').

examples.text: جيبي كيس تلج علطول وحطيه عالكاحل.
examples.trans: Grab an ice pack right away and put it on the ankle.

examples.text: امشي علطول لآخر الممر بتلاقي غرفة الشمس.
examples.trans: Walk straight down to the end of the hall and you'll find the sunroom.

meanings.note: Everyday preposition 'on, at, to'; before ال- it regularly contracts to عال- ('al- / 'a-).

examples.trans: Your glasses are on your forehead!
Say hello to Salma for me!

meanings.note: Marks location ('at, by') and with pronoun suffixes expresses possession: عندي ('I have'), عندك ('you have'), عندنا ('we have').

examples.trans: A taxi just stopped at the door.
I have a reservation under the name Suad.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: عيل.

examples.trans: The whole family gathers on Friday.
My family lived near here.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: غرف.

examples.trans: We have eight comfortable rooms at the guesthouse.
Room four is ready and clean.

meanings.note: As an adjective غريب / غريبة means 'strange, odd'; as a noun (plural غرباء) it means 'stranger(s)'.

examples.trans: I heard a strange metallic knock at night.
Why would he leave his bag with strangers?

meanings.note: After negation, ما ... غير means 'only / nothing except'.

examples.text: ما معي غير المعطف اللي علي!
examples.trans: I have nothing with me except the coat I have on!
There are only two valves on the shelf.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: فاضية, plural: فاضيين).

examples.trans: Is room six vacant tonight?
The street outside the gate is completely empty.

meanings.note: Means 'before' (قبل الفطور) and with a time span 'ago' (قبل ساعة 'an hour ago', قبل شوي 'just now').

examples.text: علمت بيانو هون قبل خمسة وعشرين سنة.
examples.trans: I taught piano here twenty-five years ago.
Drink your coffee before the rush.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: قديمة, plural: قدام).

examples.trans: The courtyard has an old jasmine tree.
The old hardware shop is past the bridge.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian form of زجاج ('glass').

examples.trans: Look at the courtyard through the window glass.
We wiped the glass this morning until it shone.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: كبيرة, plural: كبار).

examples.trans: We use this big paper ledger.
You know older brothers well!

كمان.gloss: also; too; again (كمان مرة once more)

meanings.en: also; too; again (كمان مرة once more)
meanings.note: Everyday Levantine word for 'also, too, more' (كمان مرة 'one more time / again').

examples.text: التفكير السريع أنقذ الفطور كمان مرة!
examples.trans: Quick thinking saved breakfast once again!
And I missed you too.

meanings.note: Question word 'how?'.

examples.trans: How was the bus ride?
Tell me how to find the shop.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: كيكات.

examples.text: كيكة الليمون الصفرا طلعت من الفرن.
examples.trans: The yellow lemon cake came out of the oven.
We sliced the cake into six equal pieces.

meanings.note: Attached prefix ل- before nouns ('for/to'); before pronoun suffixes in spoken Jordanian it takes the stem إل-: إلي ('for me / mine'), إلك ('for you / yours'), إله ('his'), إلها ('hers'), إلنا ('ours'), إلكم ('yours pl.').

examples.trans: The blue suitcase is mine.
Thank you all very much!

meanings.note: Versatile Jordanian noun meaning a wrapped parcel (اللفة البيضا), a pastry roll (لفة قرفة, also pl. لفائف), a street/stair turn (عاللفة), or a wrench turn (لفة، لفتين).

examples.text: أكلت لفة قرفة سخنة مع الشاي.
examples.trans: I ate a warm cinnamon roll with tea.
Watch the tight turn on the stairs.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian conjunction 'when' (in statements, not questions).

examples.trans: Smile when the bell rings!
When I get nervous, my sentences turn long.

meanings.note: Refers to a whiteboard (اللوح الأبيض), wooden plank, or windowpane (لوح قزاز).

examples.text: كتبنا مهام الأسبوع التلاتة عاللوح الأبيض.
examples.trans: We wrote the three tasks for the week on the whiteboard.

examples.text: نضفنا كل ألواح القزاز من الغبرة القديمة.
examples.trans: We cleaned all the glass panes of their old dust.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: لوحات.

examples.text: شوف لوحة المفاتيح الخشب ورا المكتب.
examples.trans: Look at the wooden key board behind the desk.
We wiped the dust off the brass plate.

meanings.note: Definite الليلة means 'tonight', while indefinite ليلة means 'one night / night of'.

examples.trans: I am going to sleep well tonight.
We booked the room for three nights.

meanings.note: Negates verbs and في (ما بعرف 'I don't know', ما في 'there isn't'), and links conjunctions like قبل ما ('before') and بعد ما ('after').

examples.trans: Paper does not lose room names.
Have tea before you head out.

meanings.note: Passive participle of بحّ ('to grow hoarse'), describing a warm, scratchy, or husky voice.

examples.text: وصوت رامي اللي لسا مبحوح شوي.
examples.trans: And Rami's voice, which is still a little hoarse.
My voice is hoarse from the cold today.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: محطات.

examples.trans: I arrived at the bus station in the morning.
The hotel is close to the station.

meanings.note: Negates nouns, adjectives, participles, and pronouns in spoken Jordanian (مش شنتتي 'not my bag', مش ملاقي 'cannot find').

examples.trans: This is not my suitcase!
Not bad for a second day at work!

meanings.note: Common defective verb for walking on foot or things running smoothly.

examples.text: ممنوع تمشي عكاحلك لحد بكرا الصبح.
examples.trans: You mustn't walk on your ankle until tomorrow morning.

examples.text: مشينا عالهدا بالساحة بعد ما وقفت المطر.
examples.trans: We walked gently across the courtyard after the rain stopped.

meanings.note: Everyday preposition 'with'; takes pronoun suffixes to express 'have on one's person' (معي 'I have with me', معك حق 'you are right').

examples.trans: You are right, Nour!
Goodbye! (lit. go with safety)

meanings.note: Means both a door key and a mechanic's spanner/wrench (مفتاح حديد iron wrench).

examples.trans: Here is the key to room four.
We have eight brass keys on the board.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: مفتوحة, plural: مفتوحين).

examples.trans: Is the hardware shop open right now?
Here is to neighbours and our open gates!

meanings.note: Passive participle of فرد ('to spread/unfold'), describing flat sheets of paper or rolled dough.

examples.trans: They stayed flat inside the box.
The papers are spread out on the table.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: ملفوفة, plural: ملفوفين).

examples.text: شو هاد الشي الملفوف بورق أبيض؟
examples.trans: What is this thing wrapped in white paper?
The parcel is wrapped with great care.

meanings.note: Placed before a subjunctive verb, ممكن makes an effortless polite request ('may I / could we?').

examples.trans: May I see the room first?
Could I see the tag in the sunlight?

meanings.note: Everyday preposition meaning 'from', 'of', or 'than' after comparatives.

examples.trans: I am Salma from the kitchen.
Breakfast is from seven-thirty to ten.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun.

examples.trans: We found an old music book in the suitcase.
Gentle music is soothing in the evening.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بنادي, بينادي).

examples.trans: Do we call each other by first name here?
Salma called everyone to breakfast.

meanings.note: In Jordanian Arabic, نحاس covers both yellow brass and red copper, often placed directly after a noun (مفاتيح نحاس brass keys).

examples.trans: We polished the brass keys in the morning.
The brass pot is old and engraved.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بنزل, بينزل).

examples.trans: Let us bring the suitcase down into the light.
Let me lower my glasses from my forehead!

meanings.note: Sound Form I verb (بهمس / همست) from root ه-م-س ('soft sound/whispering').

examples.trans: Word whispered to me that you opened the box.

examples.text: همست بإذنها عشان ما حدا يسمع.
examples.trans: She whispered in her ear so nobody would hear.

هيك.gloss: like this; so (عشان هيك that's why)

meanings.en: like this; so (عشان هيك that's why)
meanings.note: Spoken Levantine word for 'like this / that way' (عشان هيك 'that is why', مع هيك 'even so').

examples.trans: That is why the suitcase was heavy!
And after that, where do I go?

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian form of وراء ('behind, past').

examples.trans: Look in the mirror behind the desk.
The hardware shop is past the bridge.

meanings.note: Collective ورق ('paper / tree leaves'), singulative ورقة ('a sheet of paper / note'), plural أوراق ('documents / papers').

examples.trans: We use a paper ledger and a pencil.
He wrote a note on a small slip of paper.

meanings.note: Placed directly before a name or title when addressing someone in Arabic (يا نور 'Nour!', يا أستاذ 'sir!') and in exclamations (يا سلام! 'wonderful!').

examples.trans: Good morning, Tariq!
Oh, how lovely the sun is after the rain!
